subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 30-year-old man is evaluated for multiple cafe-au-lait macules, axillary freckling, and several soft cutaneous nodules. He has a family history of a similar disorder, and sequencing of the NF1 gene reveals a single nucleotide substitution that converts a coding codon into UAG in the middle of the mRNA.
question: Which type of mutation is most likely responsible for the truncated, nonfunctional neurofibromin in this patient?
explanation_correct: UAG is one of the three stop codons (UAA, UAG, and UGA). A single base substitution that converts a sense codon into a stop codon is a nonsense mutation, so translation terminates prematurely and the shortened protein is usually nonfunctional and rapidly degraded. Loss of one functional NF1 allele causes neurofibromatosis type 1.

explanation_incorrect.B: A missense mutation replaces one amino acid with another but does not create a premature stop codon, so a full-length protein would still be produced.
explanation_incorrect.C: A silent mutation does not change the amino acid and would not explain a truncated protein.
explanation_incorrect.D: A frameshift deletion changes the reading frame and alters all codons downstream; it is not a single substitution creating a stop codon at this site.
explanation_incorrect.E: A splice-site mutation causes intron retention or exon skipping during RNA processing, not replacement of a single coding codon by a stop codon.

educationalObjective: A single nucleotide change that converts a sense codon into a stop codon (UAA, UAG, or UGA) is a nonsense mutation and typically yields a truncated, nonfunctional protein.
